newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
- Corporate America won at the ballot box as voters rejected a series of state ballot initiatives designed to restrict business freedoms.
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average set a closing high for the first time since October 18, a day after the U.S. presidential elections.
- Shareholders of Wallace Computer Services Inc rejected a proposal to give them the power to decide whether to put their company for sale.
- Some food producers and supermarket chains in Europe are boycotting genetically engineered soybeans from Monsanto Co .
- CSX Corp boosted the cash protion of its bid for Conrail Inc in an effort to block attempts by Norfolk Southern Corp's to get it.
- Texaco Inc punished former and current executives for racist comments and plans to destroy documents sought in a discrimination lawsuit.
- Texas Instruments Inc is taking bids for its defense unit.
- Investor and corporate raider Bennett LeBow appears to be competing with Carl Icahn as he files his list of nominees for a new board of directors at RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
- Four members of re-elected President Bill Clinton's cabinet will resign, including Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor.
- A judge has rejected New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani's attempts to oblige Time Warner Inc cable company to carry News Corp Ltd's Fox News Channel in the city.
- United Steelworkers of America reached an agreement with Bridgestone/Firestone to end a labor dispute.
- Republicans declared victory over labor in the congressional elections, while union leaders said they managed to show their political clout.
- Czech and Slovak American Enterprise Fund will sell its Czech investments at a great loss.
